stories.headline: Fierce East Coast storm dumps 139 mm of rain and disrupts Thanksgiving travel for millions
stories.ticker: Coastal storm off Cape Hatteras sweeps **139 mm of heavy rain** ashore /// Atlantic seaboard lashed by **90 km/h wind gusts** moving north /// **States of emergency** in New York and New Jersey; parade postponed **first time in 100 years** /// Sudden flip after **two dry weeks** as **+7.3 °C Gulf Stream air** deepened a **1001 hPa low** /// RANKING: **#1 wettest late-November day in 87 years** of ERA5 records since 1940 /// CLIMATE LINK: **+3.0 °C coastal warming** since 1940-1979 has **doubled extreme rainstorms**
stories.voice_script: In the eastern United States, a powerful coastal storm is sweeping one hundred and thirty-nine millimetres of heavy rain, and gusts of ninety kilometres an hour, right up the Atlantic seaboard. States of emergency are in force across New York and New Jersey, and for the first time in a century, New York's Thanksgiving Day Parade has had to be postponed. Rather than a slow multi-week build-up, this storm marks a sudden weather flip after two dry weeks, triggered as unusually warm Gulf Stream air collided with a sharp upper trough. Across eighty-seven years of climate records back to nineteen forty, today's offshore downpour ranks number one for late November. Along this coast, late-autumn air has warmed by three degrees since the mid-twentieth century, doubling the frequency of extreme coastal rainstorms.

stories.headline: El Nino downpours bring another 184 mm deluge after rivers burst their banks in Ecuador
stories.ticker: Pacific moisture dumps **184 mm of rain in 24 hours** on Ecuador and northern Peru /// **Eight overflowing rivers** in Los Rios flood towns **two metres deep** under emergency rule /// DURATION: **25 wet days in 4 weeks**, piling up **718 mm of rain in a fortnight** /// RANKING: Unprecedented **#1 for late November** across **87 years** of ERA5 data since 1940 /// CLIMATE LINK: **2026 El Nino** plus **+1.4 °C warming** has **doubled extreme November deluges**
stories.voice_script: In South America, torrential Pacific moisture banking against the western Andes is pouring another one hundred and eighty-four millimetres of rain onto coastal Ecuador and northern Peru. Eight rivers have already burst their banks in western Ecuador, flooding neighbourhoods up to two metres deep and forcing local states of emergency. Crucially, this crisis has been building all month: twenty-five of the past twenty-eight days have brought heavy rain, piling up over seven hundred millimetres in just a fortnight. In eighty-seven years of records since nineteen forty, this rainfall rate is completely unprecedented, ranking number one for late November. Alongside a strengthening El Nino, coastal air here has warmed by one point four degrees since the mid-twentieth century, doubling the odds of extreme November downpours.

stories.headline: Fresh 137 mm Adriatic storm hits flood-weary Italy and the Balkans after weeks of rain
stories.ticker: Southerly gales of **90 km/h** drive warm Mediterranean moisture into the Adriatic /// Fresh **137 mm downpour in 24 hours** hits Croatia and Montenegro /// Follows **Storm Charles river evacuations** in northern Italy and coastal flooding in Split /// DURATION & RANK: **676 mm across 10 storm days**, ranking **4th wettest since 1940** /// CLIMATE LINK: **+1.4 °C Adriatic warming** since 1940-1979 has **tripled severe autumn rains**
stories.voice_script: Across southern Europe, southerly gales of ninety kilometres an hour are driving warm Mediterranean air straight into the Adriatic coast, unleashing another one hundred and thirty-seven millimetres of rain across Croatia and Montenegro. It arrives just days after Storm Charles forced river evacuations in northern Italy and flooded historic seafronts along the Dalmatian coast. The ground here can hold no more water: ten of the last fourteen days have brought heavy storms, totalling nearly seven hundred millimetres in two weeks. Looking back to nineteen forty, today ranks fourth wettest on record for late November. As the Mediterranean has warmed by one point four degrees since the mid-twentieth century, severe late-autumn downpours along this coast have tripled.

stories.headline: Giant Eurasian heat dome pushes late-November temperatures up to 19 °C above normal
stories.ticker: Vast **Eurasian warm dome** from Kazakhstan to central Siberia flips winter upside down /// Kazakhstan hits **+14.0 °C (+16.4 °C anomaly)** while Siberia sits **+19.8 °C above normal** /// DURATION: Stubborn **blocking high** keeps **all 28 of the past 28 days** anomalously warm /// RANKING: Steppe warmth stands **#1 on record (99.4th percentile)** since 1940 /// CLIMATE LINK: **+2.4 °C Siberian warming** since 1940-1979 has **doubled extreme autumn thaws**
stories.voice_script: Turning to Eurasia, an extraordinary dome of warm air stretching from Kazakhstan into central Siberia has turned deep winter upside down. Afternoon temperatures in southeastern Kazakhstan have reached fourteen degrees, more than sixteen degrees above normal, while northern Siberia sits nearly twenty degrees warmer than the late-November average. Remarkably, this blocking high has held firm for four straight weeks, with all twenty-eight of the past twenty-eight days in southeastern Kazakhstan running warmer than normal. Across eighty-seven years of records since nineteen forty, this steppe warmth stands at number one on record. Northern Siberia has warmed by two point four degrees in late November since the mid-twentieth century, doubling the likelihood of extreme autumn thaws as snow cover retreats.

stories.headline: Powerful 975 hPa North Atlantic storm blasts Iceland with 133 km/h gales and sweeps rain into Ireland
stories.ticker: Deep North Atlantic storm batters southern Iceland with **133 km/h violent gusts** /// Heavy rainbands sweep **eight Irish counties under Met Eireann warnings** and SW England /// DURATION: **975 hPa storm track** brings **9 gale days in 2 weeks** and **229 mm in 28 days** /// RANKING: Gusts **double the seasonal norm**, ranking in the **top 1% since 1940** /// CLIMATE LINK: **+1.6 °C warming** and a **+4.5 °C plume** turn winter snow into **flooding rain**
stories.voice_script: Finally, in the North Atlantic, a deep storm system is battering southern Iceland with violent gusts of one hundred and thirty-three kilometres an hour, while sweeping bands of heavy wind and rain across Ireland and western Britain. Eight Irish counties have been placed under weather warnings by Met Eireann, alongside flood alerts in south-west England. An energetic jet stream has aimed storm after storm along this corridor, bringing nine gale days in the past fortnight and over two hundred millimetres of rain in four weeks. Peak gusts near Iceland are more than double the late-November average, ranking in the top one percent of storms since nineteen forty. And with regional temperatures one point six degrees warmer than in the mid-twentieth century, moisture that once fell as early-winter snow increasingly falls as heavy, flood-producing rain.
